title: The AMPLIFY brief
blurb: Your first week at Northline. Win trust, handle a rival, and deliver for AMPLIFY.

preGame.handoffLine: Your first week at Northline starts now.

screens.heading: Help people finish a task.
screens.body: UX means user experience. Designers study what people need, then test ways to help.

screens.heading: Start rough. Learn fast.
screens.body: A wireframe is a rough screen layout. A prototype is a test version of a design.

screens.heading: Try it.
screens.question: What should guide a design change?

options.label: What people need and what tests show
options.why: Evidence helps the team choose what to improve.

options.label: Which color the designer likes best
options.why: Personal taste does not show whether a task works.

preGame.missionLine: Build your skills. Design careers can follow different paths.

ladderBranches.label: Management path
ladderBranches.roles: Design Manager → Director → VP of Design

preGame.ladderNote: Titles vary by company. These are career paths, not promised promotions.

endings.headline: Your next assignment is earned.
endings.scoreNote: You earn a place on the next project.
endings.message: Samira wants you on the next client team. Arjun stays your guide, and Noah will be working alongside you.
endings.subline: Level 1 complete. The next chapter is planned, not playable yet.

endings.headline: Revise and retry
endings.message: Arjun asks you to try again. Check the brief, use the evidence, and ask for help before the deadline.
endings.subline: Replay Level 1 with what you learned.

endings.headline: This attempt ends here
endings.message: Take a fresh run and use what you learned.
endings.subline: One attempt does not define your future.

scoreTip: Start at 50. Seven scored decisions change reputation by 6. Matching practice does not change your score. Reach 85.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Welcome to UX Design.
beats.body: Your first week at Northline starts today. Your team builds a music-app demo for AMPLIFY.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: One week. One place on the next project.
beats.body: AMPLIFY reviews the work Friday. Both juniors want to join the next client team. Your decisions will shape who gets trusted.

beats.speaker: Arjun
beats.title: Arjun has your first assignment.
beats.body: Arjun is a senior UX designer. He guides your work and reviews it before it reaches the client.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Your work goes through Arjun.
beats.body: Sketch a rough layout before polishing it. Arjun reviews changes and test plans. Ask him about priorities or problems before the client sees your work.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Another junior starts beside you.
beats.body: Noah is working on AMPLIFY too. You exchange a quick hello before the first assignment.

beats.speaker: Arjun
beats.question: Arjun asks for a rough screen plan before any polish. What should you make?

choices.label: A wireframe showing the main layout.
choices.why: A wireframe lets the team review the layout before spending time on polish.

choices.label: A finished app with every screen built.
choices.why: The layout needs review before the team builds the finished app.

choices.label: A new logo for the client.
choices.why: The assignment is the screen layout, not the brand identity.

beats.planLineIfFailed: you missed a step the team needed

beats.speaker: Arjun
beats.title: Four words for your first assignment.
beats.setup: These tools help you sketch, test, and record what fans actually do.

cards.def: Watch a person try a goal without hints
What someone did or said, without guessing why

beats.speaker: Arjun
beats.setup: Arjun shares the plan for the AMPLIFY test.
beats.question: Match each design job to the right tool.

pairs.term: Let a fan try the Save flow.
See if a fan can keep a set.

beats.whenRight: Each tool has a job in the design process.
beats.whenWrong: Match the work to the tool, not just a similar word.

beats.speaker: Arjun
beats.setup: Arjun checks your plan before the first fan session.

items.question: You need a quick layout before choosing colors. Which tool fits?

options.label: Wireframe.
options.why: It shows structure before visual polish.

options.label: Finished app.
options.why: A finished app is more work than this first sketch needs.

options.label: Logo sheet.
options.why: A logo does not show the screen layout.

items.question: A fan needs to try moving between screens. What should you prepare?

options.label: A linked prototype.
options.why: A prototype lets a person try the flow.

options.label: A list of brand colors.
options.why: Colors alone do not let someone try the flow.

options.label: A page of meeting notes.
options.why: Notes record work but do not simulate the flow.

items.question: A fan pauses, then asks where Save is. Which note is an observation?

options.label: Paused, then asked where Save is.
options.why: This records what the fan did and said.

options.label: The fan dislikes music.
options.why: You did not observe that preference.

options.label: Everyone will miss Save.
options.why: One observation does not establish what everyone will do.

items.question: Which request tests the design without giving a hint?

options.label: Keep this set so you can find it later.
options.why: It gives a goal without naming the control.

options.label: Press Save beside the title.
options.why: That tells the fan where the control is.

options.label: You can see Save, right?
options.why: That points out the answer instead of testing discovery.

beats.whenPass: Your plan uses the right tools and lets fans act without hints.
beats.whenFail: Use rough layouts, testable prototypes, and notes about what people actually do.
beats.planLineIfFailed: you missed a step the team needed

beats.speaker: Arjun
beats.title: Put the main action near its content.
beats.body: Fans miss Save below a long description. Sketch a clearer position near the set it affects. Arjun reviews the prototype before anyone publishes it.

artifact.title: Current layout
artifact.caption: Current AMPLIFY layout: Save sits below a long description.
artifact.provenance: Fictional layout matching the problem stated in the task.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.question: Fans miss Save below a long description. Where should you place it in the next prototype?

choices.label: Beside the set title.
choices.why: The action stays close to the set it saves and above the long copy.

choices.label: Below an even longer description.
choices.why: More copy keeps the same discovery problem.

choices.label: Inside a new hidden menu.
choices.why: Hiding the main action adds another step.

beats.speaker: Samira
beats.title: Samira arrives for the client review.
beats.body: The Design Lead needs a clear, accurate report before the client sees it.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: A clearer layout still needs a test.
beats.body: The goal is to keep a set for later. Give that goal without naming Save or pointing. Record whether the fan finishes without help.

artifact.title: Proposed layout
artifact.caption: Proposed AMPLIFY layout: Save sits beside the set title. It still needs testing.
artifact.provenance: Fictional prototype proposal, not a claim of improved test results.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Samira chooses the next client team.
beats.body: Arjun reviews your work. Samira looks for sound judgment and clear evidence before giving you more responsibility.

beats.speaker: Samira
beats.question: Which task should you give a fan to test the revised Save layout?

choices.label: Keep this set so you can find it tomorrow.
choices.why: The goal is clear without telling the fan where to click.

choices.label: Click Save beside the title.
choices.why: That gives away the control you need to test.

choices.label: Do you like the new colors?
choices.why: That asks about preference, not whether the Save task works.

choices.label: Watch me save this set, then copy me.
choices.why: A demonstration hides whether the fan can find the action alone.

beats.planLineIfFailed: you missed a step the team needed

artifact.title: Proposed layout
artifact.caption: Proposed AMPLIFY layout: Save sits beside the set title. It still needs testing.
artifact.provenance: Fictional prototype proposal, not a claim of improved test results.

intro.line: Arjun and Samira review your first decisions.

pass.title: You passed the first review.
pass.body: The next client assignment is still yours to earn.

fail.title: You can still turn this around.
fail.body: Use the feedback in the second half.

beats.speaker: System
beats.title: The second half of your first week.
beats.body: The report is taking shape. Now the pressure shifts to the team.

beats.speaker: Noah
beats.title: Noah wants that next assignment too.
beats.body: Noah is quick and confident. The client review is a chance to stand out, and sharing credit is not the plan.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: The next morning, you hear your work claimed.
beats.body: You wrote the test findings. Now Noah tells Samira, “I put that report together.” Your saved file shows your work.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.question: Noah took credit for your report. What should you do?

choices.label: Share the file history with Arjun privately.
choices.why: Use the record and the right person without turning it into a public fight.

choices.label: Accuse Noah in front of the client.
choices.why: A client meeting is not the place to settle a team dispute.

choices.label: Post about it online.
choices.why: That exposes private work and makes the conflict public.

choices.label: Change the report to make the rival look bad.
choices.why: Sabotage damages the client’s work and your own trust.

beats.planLineIfFailed: you missed a step the team needed

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: 3:00 P.M. The Save link breaks.
beats.body: Save opens the wrong screen. The cover art also needs polish. Only one fix fits before the 6:00 client review. Arjun must agree to the priority.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.question: Only one fix fits before six. What should you propose to Arjun?

choices.label: Fix the Save path first; leave cover art rough.
choices.why: The client needs to try the core task. Arjun can approve leaving polish for later.

choices.label: Polish the cover art and hide the broken link.
choices.why: A polished screen does not fix the task the client needs to try.

choices.label: Add more screens before checking Save.
choices.why: More screens increase work while the core path remains broken.

beats.planLineIfFailed: you missed a step the team needed

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: 6:00 P.M. The review pack is ready.
beats.body: Arjun reviews the repaired Save path. Cover art stays rough. The client can try the main task; the next test will show what still needs work.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Amina still needs a hand.
beats.body: Amina, an accessibility specialist, needs keyboard-check notes by 6:40. You have finished your work. She owns the final check.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Help with the notes, not the sign-off.
beats.body: Amina asks you to record where keyboard focus stops. Send her those notes. She decides what needs fixing before any accessibility claim.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.question: Amina needs keyboard-check notes. Rank your responses from best to worst.
order: Record where focus stops and send Amina the notes.
Offer to polish cover art instead.
Mark the screen accessible without a check.
beats.whenRight: You support the actual check and leave final judgment with the specialist.
beats.whenWrong: Useful notes help Amina. Unrelated polish and untested claims do not.
beats.planLineIfFailed: you missed a step the team needed

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Arjun noticed how you handled it.
beats.body: Your response under pressure matters, even when the client is not watching.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Your first week is complete.
beats.body: Arjun sends your work to Samira. The next assignment depends on the trust you built this week.

beats.speaker: System
beats.title: Northline is choosing the next project team.
beats.body: Your reputation helps decide what happens next.
beats.decidingNote: The team reviews your work and how you handled pressure.
